prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: one portrait illustration for the 1971 chapter of a Jackie Leven homage website, designed to sit on a near-black background.
Primary request: create a new, recognizable portrait of the YOUNG Jackie Leven around 1971, using the two historical photos for his actual early-era facial likeness and the third image only for the established illustration style. This is the next image in a coherent series.
Input images: Image 1 (1971/img.png) is the principal facial identity reference: young face, long centre-parted hair, straight prominent nose, heavy brows, restrained moustache and small chin beard. Image 2 (1971/img_1.png) is a supporting identity/hairstyle reference from the same early period, NOT a source of printed page design. Image 3 (1977 dark illustration) is ONLY the style and tonal-value reference; do not copy its later haircut, clean-shaven face or pose.
Subject and likeness: faithfully retain the distinctive facial proportions of images 1 and 2, including his eyes, brows, nose, mouth and jaw. Early twenties; natural, unidealized features, thin moustache and short chin beard with lightly shadowed jaw, very long loose centre-parted hair reaching well beyond his shoulders. Do not turn him into a generic handsome folk singer or a different person. No ageing, no large full beard.
Composition: a NEW original chest-up composition in a vertical 4:5 frame. Torso turned slightly toward the viewer's right, head almost frontal with a small rightward turn; eyes looking just past the viewer toward the right. Face not in the same exact photographic pose. Both hands out of frame, neither hand touching his face. Relaxed but self-possessed shoulders, quiet intensity, closed neutral mouth, no smile. Simple dark open-collar shirt, only suggested by a few strokes. Keep the entire head and long hair within frame with breathing room. Lower chest and shoulders break up into unpainted darkness. The face is the visual anchor.
Style/medium: same restrained dark dry-brush ink portrait language as image 3. Bold broken strokes and broad simplified light/shadow planes. Strong abstraction in hair and clothing, recognizable facial anatomy. A small number of expressive economical strokes instead of many tiny lines. Do not increase the level of detail beyond image 3. Matte printed-ink character, subtle dry brush grain, no glossy oil-paint impasto, no photographic skin detail.
Backdrop and palette: near-black anthracite #0d0f12, monochrome dark charcoal and muted slate-grey. The portrait emerges quietly from the darkness like a subdued watermark, yet the eyes, nose and mouth remain readable. Brightest facial planes only muted medium grey, never white. Natural light/shadow logic, NOT an inverted photograph. Hair is mostly dark negative space with sparse broad grey marks, shirt nearly disappears. Outer edges and corners merge into flat anthracite for seamless placement on the webpage. Match the visual contrast of image 3.
Constraints: one single portrait, no panels, no text, no lettering, no page borders, no signature, no watermark logo. No original photo background, no page reproduction, no hand-to-temple gesture, no added instruments, no objects or other people. Preserve facial likeness while inventing the pose and composition.
